newsitem.title: UK: Product tanker rates steady, no Iraqi impact.
newsitem.headline: Product tanker rates steady, no Iraqi impact.

text.p: Clean tanker rates in most major lifting sectors settled on previous done levels amid thinner activity, brokers said on Friday.
Middle East activity was sluggish with rates on 55,000 tonners to Japan resting at W167.5. The U.S. confrontation with Iraqi has not impacted on the market.
London brokers said the market was reasonably dormant and they expected rates to remain flat until the end of September.
Neither 70,000 nor 55,000 tonners were seen done, and by the close of Friday, only two vessels had been fixed. Both these cargoes, 43,000 and 44,000 tonnes apiece were headed to India.
Demand in the UK/Continent sector for 20,000 tonners was extremely thin, brokers said.
A single 27,000 tonne cargo fixed by Addax on the Scarlet Star was seen fixed out of Le Havre for Nigeria.
"Owners plying the inter-UKC market have had the opportunity to put slight pressure on freight rates and 22,000 tonne eventually paid W202.5 this week," shipbrokers Gibsons said in a report.

Brokers said rates in the Caribbean up U.S market were put at W185 compared with last week's W225, despite an improvement in fixing. Tonnage has been thinned and some brokers see potential for rate gains next week.
In the Mediterranean chartering improved slightly during the course of the week with 30,000 gas oil carriers taking W130 while naphtha suitable tonnage has been able to command W165 on 27,500 tonnes.
